## Methodology
A commander-role row clears the written statistical bar only when DEDUPED N >= 40, the commander's P25 is >= 1.5x or <= 0.667x the corpus P25 (or differs by at least 2.0 cards when the corpus P25 is zero), and |z| >= 2.0; z is computed as (commanderMean - corpusMean) / (corpusStdDev / sqrt(n)).
RAW N is the count of distinct reconstructed mainboard deck_queue ids for a commander before content-hash collapse; DEDUPED N collapses same-content_hash near-duplicates to one representative deck per non-null hash, so DEDUPED N is the only N compared against the threshold or passed into ClearsFloorBar.
Every card is classified oracle-only with the production role assigner using empty categories and `isComboPiece: false`: categories are intentionally always `[]` because `PlanRoleClassifier.Classify` is categories-first and first-hit-wins, so using live Archidekt tags would partially measure each commander playerbase's tagging habits rather than the card's mechanics. This matches the already-shipped `CutLabSimulationService.cs:517` call shape, but it means these findings do not reproduce what CutLabRoleAssigner outputs today for an actually-tagged production decklist.
The verdict is computed from the commander's 25th percentile against the corpus 25th percentile; the mean z-score is retained only as a significance gate because a sample percentile has no closed-form standard error.
When the corpus P25 is zero, the multiplicative ratio is undefined and `ComputeRatio` returns 0.0, so the bar falls back to an absolute gap of 2.0 cards; that is the smallest floor difference worth stating as a recommendation.
EDHREC cells never enter the go/no-go, because ClearsFloorBar requires a standard deviation and a sample size that a single synthesized average deck cannot supply.
Cohen's d is reported alongside ratio and z as a scale-uniform effect size, because a fixed 1.5x / 0.667x ratio gate is not scale-fair across roles with very different corpus-wide means.
A role is only a Phase-2 "go" when at least 3 distinct qualifying commanders clear the bar in that role; one or two clearing commanders is recorded as signal present but insufficient breadth.
At these defaults the z-gate is largely redundant once N and ratio are both satisfied: for example, N=40, sd=3, mean=6, and a 1.5x ratio implies z~6.3, far above the 2.0 cutoff.
This run reconstructed 130075 raw mainboard decks, 128407 deduped representative decks, enumerated 4011 commanders, and retained 841 qualifying commanders at the primary DEDUPED-N threshold of 40.
Unresolved Scryfall card names excluded from tallies: 14 total (14 not_found, 0 rate_limited_after_retry).

Known gaps:
- Card-level category-tag coverage gap: a tagged deck can still leave individual cards uncategorized, so reconstructed decklists may miss cards.
- Deck-level invisibility gap: a processed deck with zero category-tagged cards contributes no membership rows at all and is invisible to this pipeline.
- content_hash NULL dedup limitation: dedup is conservative, not perfect, because older deck_queue rows may still have NULL content_hash values.
- `isComboPiece` is fixed to `false`, so combo-only win conditions can be undercounted.
- ManabaseMode is fixed per run, so this pass does not compare role floors across multiple play-experience modes.
- The `other` residual role is deliberately excluded because it measures fallback classifier coverage rather than deck-construction structure.
- Postgres decks are classified as singleton card sets because Commander is singleton for the target nonland roles there, while EDHREC cells preserve real decklist quantities so basics and other repeated entries are counted at their actual quantity.
- Oracle-only classification means these findings do not reproduce today's category-aware production role output for a tagged decklist.
- Cards that still fail after harness-side HTTP 429 retry are tracked separately as `rate_limited_after_retry`; like true `not_found` names, they are excluded from classification tallies, but this run distinguishes the two unresolved reasons.
- EDHREC quantity-parse failures excluded rather than dropped silently: 0 raw deck entries across all ingested cells failed the quantity-prefix parse and were left out of classification.
- EDHREC parsed-card-count anomalies: 31 ingested cells did not sum to 100 parsed cards after quantity parsing.
- `boardFilter: "mainboard"` commander-membership exclusion of `sideboard` and `maybeboard` rows is verified by `CategoryCacheSchemaParityTests.GetCategoryDeckMembershipForCommanderAsync_BoardFilterMainboard_ExcludesSideboardAndMaybeboardRows`.
- Protection under-detection disclosure (unconditional): see `## Go/No-Go` below for the full disclosure; this run's protection floors are a LOWER BOUND and any protection verdict is PROVISIONAL pending Phase 01.2. `DeckStatClassifier.IsProtectionCard` (`DeckFlow.Core/Analysis/DeckStatClassifier.cs:226-231`) is `StaxProtectionCatalog.IsProtection(name)` OR-ed with four oracle needles:
### Corpus hygiene disclosure
Corpus scale: 397,063 decks, 151,202 processed, 4,003 commanders with processed decks. Depth: 847 commanders at >=40 decks, 346 at >=100, 88 at >=250, 17 at >=500, deepest 917.
From a random sample of n=300 processed decks drawn across commanders clearing the >=40 gate: 286/287 live decks are `deckFormat` 3 (Commander), 99.65% (one was format 7); 13/300 (4.3%) deck ids are dead — 404, private, or deleted; 7/287 (2.4%) live decks are `theorycrafted`. Created-year spread: 213x 2026, 62x 2025, 10x 2024, 1x 2023, 1x 2021.
There is no recency window. Decks are counted regardless of age, and the corpus carries no `createdAt` or `updatedAt` at all — the year figures above come from the sample's live API responses, not from stored data.
The 4.3% dead-id rate inflates every deck count in this document, including the deduped counts the go/no-go breadth bar is applied against.
`ArchidektApiDeckImporter` parses `cards[]` only. `deckFormat`, `theorycrafted`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `viewCount`, `points`, `edhBracket` are unparsed and unstored, so commander-ness is inferred from a card categorized `Commander`, never from the deck's declared format.
This is a stated limitation, not a blocker. Phase 5 remains independent and non-gating: `edhBracket` is present on the payload at roughly 25% fill and is free to capture, but the deepest commander has 917 decks, so 917 x 25% / 5 brackets is roughly 46 decks per cell against EDHREC's 400 floor. Archidekt bracket capture therefore cannot fill a bracket cell for any commander, now or after a full backfill. That arithmetic strengthens decision D-A rather than weakening it.
By contrast, the EDHREC side does carry a recency window through each cell's `savedate_summary`; this run observed an overall range of 2024-07-28 to 2026-07-27.

## Lands Calibration Control
**Verdict vs the 2026-07-16 prior: contradicts**
The prior in `.planning/archive/2026-cycles/research/2026-07-16-edhrec-bracket-land-data.md` concluded that bracket drove land count, commander identity barely moved it, and every commander-ability-driven land adjustment was rejected; on this control role that means a lands `no-go` reproduces the prior while a lands `go` contradicts it.

| Bracket | Prior mean / SD | Live shipped avgLands | Fresh measured avgLands |
|---------|-----------------:|----------------------:|------------------------:|
| B1 | 36.3 / 2.24 | n/a (no B1 row in the snapshot) | n/a (insufficient cells) |
| B2 | 35.7 / 1.19 | 35.9 | 36.127 |
| B3 | 35.2 / 1.25 | 35.5 | 35.748 |
| B4 | 34.5 / 1.2 | 34.5 | 34.594 |
| B5 | 30 / 2.14 | 30.5 | 29.1 (40 qualifying cells) |
Postgres corpus-wide only (not bracket-resolved; the Postgres corpus has no bracket dimension): mean / SD / P25 = 18.354 / 10.497 / 10.
**Do the three reference sets agree?** Maximum absolute spread across prior / live / fresh = 1.4 lands; brackets exceeding a 1.0-land spread: B5. Using this run's Postgres mean (18.354) as the only comparable scalar from the within-commander corpus, it sits closest on average to the prior, computed over B2-B5 (brackets where all three sets carry a value). Agreement among the three EDHREC-derived baselines says nothing about this run's Postgres P25 result, which measures a quantity none of them can measure.

This contradicts the prior, so per the ROADMAP this is a finding about the methodology before it is a finding about decks. First suspects: the P25-versus-point-estimate difference, the EDHREC land self-check deltas from plan 02-06, and the Postgres corpus category-tag coverage gaps already listed in Known gaps.

### Ramp — no prior to compare against
Per-commander ramp variation was never measured this way in the 2026-07-16 work. That study addressed commander-ability-driven land adjustment, which is a different question, so this run's ramp verdict stands on its own with no reproduce/contradict comparison available.

## Go/No-Go
**Roles in scope for Phase 3:** lands, ramp, draw, interaction-targeted, engines, payoffs, wincons
**Signal present but insufficient breadth (NOT in scope):** interaction-mass, protection
### The casual-bias objection
Archived conclusion: EDHREC averages are casual-dominated (`.planning/archive/2026-cycles/quick/260718-nip-investigate-usefulness-of-edhrec-dump-fo/`).
The codebase already acted on that conclusion in two places: `ManabaseAnalysisService.cs:603-605` restricts the EDHREC commander cell to brackets 2-3, and `CutLabFloorDefaults.ResolveLandsDefault` routes bracket 5 to the cEDH tournament corpus instead.
The objection aimed at this phase's premise is that a stax deck and a swarm deck under the same commander are both correct with wildly different mixes, so distance-from-average is noise for the serious-builder audience.
This run says, using `Avg_role(Avg_commander(max(0, commanderMean - commanderP25)) / PopStdDev_commander(commanderMean))`, that the lower-tail within-commander spread relative to the between-commander spread is 1.128 on average across roles (lands=0.899, ramp=1.108, draw=1.122, interaction-targeted=1.208, interaction-mass=1.28, protection=1.29, engines=1.252, payoffs=0.962, wincons=1.028). That is evidence about lower-tail spread in the measured Postgres corpus, not a rebuttal of the broader claim.
What this run cannot say is whether the full within-commander archetype spread is multimodal in a way the mean/P25 summary hides; it only speaks to lower-tail spread visible in the Postgres per-deck distributions.
- lands: go (Y'shtola, Night's Blessed, Teval, the Balanced Scale, Fire Lord Azula, Toph, the First Metalbender, Krenko, Mob Boss; top 5 of 411 clearing commanders)
- ramp: go (Fire Lord Azula, Witherbloom, the Balancer, Toph, the First Metalbender, The Ur-Dragon, Hearthhull, the Worldseed; top 5 of 277 clearing commanders)
- draw: go (Y'shtola, Night's Blessed, Fire Lord Azula, Krenko, Mob Boss, The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl, Ms. Bumbleflower; top 5 of 275 clearing commanders)
- interaction-targeted: go (Y'shtola, Night's Blessed, Fire Lord Azula, The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl, The Ur-Dragon, Vivi Ornitier; top 5 of 273 clearing commanders)
- interaction-mass: signal present but insufficient breadth (Umbris, Fear Manifest)
- protection: signal present but insufficient breadth (Sergeant John Benton)

### Protection under-detection disclosure
`DeckStatClassifier.IsProtectionCard` (`DeckFlow.Core/Analysis/DeckStatClassifier.cs:226-231`) is `StaxProtectionCatalog.IsProtection(name)` OR-ed with four oracle needles:
- `gains hexproof` assumes a singular subject and misses `creatures you control gain hexproof`.
- `gains indestructible` assumes a singular subject and misses `permanents you control gain indestructible`.
- `gain protection from` assumes a plural subject and misses `Mother of Runes' target creature gains protection from the color of your choice until end of turn.`.
- `phases out` assumes a singular subject and misses `permanents you control phase out`.
The verb agreement is inconsistent across the four needles, so the predicate under-detects in both directions depending on phrasing. Shroud and regeneration are absent entirely.
Cards still scoring `PlanRole.None` after Phase 01.1, with evidence grade stated rather than flattened:
- `Swiftfoot Boots` — measured. Measured through a scratch dotnet harness against the repo code.
- `Mother of Runes` — measured. Measured through the same scratch dotnet harness against the repo code.
- `Hexing Squelcher` — measured. Measured local corpus oracle/type data from _role-floor-research/cards_full.json.
- `Goblin Chirurgeon` — measured. Measured local corpus oracle/type data from _role-floor-research/cards_full.json.
- `Lightning Greaves` — inferred. Inferred, not measured: the delta used the plan-provided oracle text and a reasoned Artifact — Equipment type line because no local facts entry for that card was present in the measured corpus files used here.
The distinction is recorded because this disclosure is the price of deferring Phase 01.2, and presenting an inferred result as measured would overstate the very evidence that deferral rests on (`.planning/workstreams/cycle21-cut-lab/phases/01.1-plan-role-classifier-heuristic-fixes-fix-the-counters-counte/01.1-02-DELTA.md`, Measurement notes).
The `protection` role's measured floors in this run are a LOWER BOUND, and any protection go/no-go verdict is PROVISIONAL pending Phase 01.2.
Phase 01.2 was deliberately deferred behind this phase by developer decision on 2026-07-27, taking the ROADMAP's escape hatch in exchange for this disclosure.
The predicate is shared by three consumers, so widening it is a larger blast radius than a one-line fix: InteractionAuditAggregator.cs:58, CutLabRoleAssigner.cs:165, PlanRoleClassifier.cs:236.
- engines: go (Fire Lord Azula, Witherbloom, the Balancer, Blech, Loafing Pest, Krenko, Mob Boss, The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl; top 5 of 379 clearing commanders)
- payoffs: go (Blech, Loafing Pest, Edgar Markov, Cloud, Ex-SOLDIER, Chatterfang, Squirrel General, Dina, Essence Brewer; top 5 of 124 clearing commanders)
- wincons: go (Blech, Loafing Pest, Edgar Markov, Cloud, Ex-SOLDIER, Chatterfang, Squirrel General, Dina, Essence Brewer; top 5 of 153 clearing commanders)
